Ziph (son of Mesha)
ZIF
proper noun
Hebrew Zīph (H2128), perhaps “refining” or “flowing,” a son in the Calebite line of Judah, fathered by Mesha (1Chr 2:42); the man, distinct from the wilderness town of the same name.

Biblical Definition

Ziph is a son in the Calebite branch of the tribe of Judah, named as the offspring of Mesha the firstborn of Caleb: “Mesha his firstborn, which was the father of Ziph” (1Chr 2:42). The reader must hold the man apart from the place, for the same name belongs to the wilderness town of Ziph in the south of Judah, in whose thickets David hid from Saul, and whose men twice came up to betray him (1Sa 23:14-15; 1Sa 26:1; Psa 54:title). The town was very likely named for this man or his house; the genealogy gives us the father, the histories give us the place that took his name. A second Ziph appears among the sons of Jehaleleel in the same chapter’s neighbourhood of registers (1Chr 4:16), a witness to how a name was kept and passed within the families of Judah. The Chronicler does not pause to tell us a single deed of this Ziph; he is content to write the name and pass on. And that is the point of the whole register: the tribe of promise is numbered name by name, generation by generation, that the line might be kept whole unto the coming of Him who should spring out of Juda (Heb 7:14). The LORD knoweth them that are His (2Ti 2:19); even the bare name in the book is precious to Him who writes the book of remembrance (Mal 3:16).

Webster 1828 Definition

A son in the Calebite line of Judah, fathered by Mesha, distinct from the wilderness town of the same name.

expand to see more

ZIPH, a son in the Calebite branch of Judah, the offspring of Mesha the firstborn of Caleb.

The name may signify “refining” or “flowing.”

He is the man, to be distinguished from the wilderness town of Ziph where David hid from Saul.

A second Ziph is reckoned among the sons of Jehaleleel in the same register of Judah.

His name is kept by the Chronicler among the households of the tribe of promise.

Key Scripture

1Chr 2:42 — "Now the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were, Mesha his firstborn, which was the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron."

1Sa 23:14 — "And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand."

2Ti 2:19 — "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."

Heb 7:14 — "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

Modern Corruption

A man of Scripture’s register, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses that the LORD numbers and names His people.

expand to see more

Ziph the son of Mesha is a name in the genealogy of Judah, and no movement of the present age has set itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him that the reader may know him for the man, and not mistake him for the wilderness town of Ziph where David hid, nor for the second Ziph among the sons of Jehaleleel.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD knoweth them that are His and keeps their names (2Ti 2:19; Luk 10:20). A man may leave behind only a town that bears his name and a line in a register; yet God forgets none of His own, and writes their names in heaven where no betrayer can blot them out.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “refining” or “flowing,” Ziph names a son in the Calebite line of Judah.

Ziph — Hebrew Zīph (H2128), perhaps “refining” or “flowing.”

He was a son in the Calebite branch of Judah, fathered by Mesha.

The wilderness town of Ziph, where David hid from Saul, likely took its name from him or his house.

A second Ziph is reckoned among the sons of Jehaleleel (1Chr 4:16).

His name is kept among the households of the tribe of promise.

Usage

"Like Ziph, a man may be remembered only by a name and a town, yet the LORD remembers him whole."

"The bare name in the register is not bare to God, who writes His people’s names in heaven."

"Names betrayed and forgotten among men are kept secure in the book of remembrance."
